Source. The exact witness classifies into 62 explicit controls (`LRO`, 33x `LRE`, `LRO`, 27x `LRE`) followed by `LTR` for `0x20202020`, `FSI` for `U+2068`, `ON` for `U+2020`, `BS` for `U+000A`, and `LTR` for `0xFFFFFF20`. `gen.tab/gen-bidi-type-tab.c` initializes the bidi table to `LTR`, and `gen.tab/packtab.c` emits `FRIBIDI_GET_BIDI_TYPE(x)` to return that default when `x >= 0x110000`, which is why the out-of-range tail word becomes the final `LTR` run.

The witness tail's bracket state is materialized here. `pre_ltr`, `fsi`, `newline`, and `post_ltr` are not `ON`, so line 91 stores `FRIBIDI_NO_BRACKET` for them directly. `dagger` is `ON`, but `gen.tab/gen-brackets-type-tab.c` defaults the bracket-type table to 0 and `gen.tab/unidata/BidiBrackets.txt` has no `2020` entry, so `fribidi_get_bracket(U+2020)` also yields `FRIBIDI_NO_BRACKET`.

FriBidi materializes those entries as heap `FriBidiRun` nodes. After the explicit-control prefix, the witness tail is five single-character runs in list order: `pre_ltr(0x20202020)`, `fsi(U+2068)`, `dagger(U+2020)`, `newline(U+000A)`, and `post_ltr(0xFFFFFF20)`; `new_run()` at `lib/fribidi-run.c:44` allocates each node, `FRIBIDI_IS_ISOLATE(char_type)` keeps `fsi` in its own run, and line 147 copies step 2's all-`FRIBIDI_NO_BRACKET` tail bracket state into the run fields.

The 62 leading `LRO/LRE` runs are all accepted explicit pushes. Starting from base level 0, these lines raise the current embedding state by 2 per run until the tail segment is reached with `level == 124`: `pre_ltr` is processed at that even level and the later `fsi` still sees the same 124 state. This is the 125-level boundary condition called out by the fix commit.

When the `fsi` run is processed, `for_run_list (fsi_pp, pp)` begins at `pp->next`, so the scan skips the FSI itself, sees `dagger` (`ON`) and `newline` (`BS`) as non-letters, then reaches `post_ltr`, whose `LTR` type from step 1 makes line 752 set `fsi_base_level = 0`. These lines therefore compute `new_level = 126`, store the FSI run itself as `RL_LEVEL=124, RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL=0`, increment `isolate_level` to 1 for following runs, and then refuse to push because 126 exceeds max 125; the following `dagger` run therefore inherits level 124 in isolate level 1.

The `newline` run is `FRIBIDI_TYPE_BS`, so explicit-level processing breaks here before writing the current level 124 into it. `newline` therefore keeps its initialized `level` 0 while retaining `RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL=1` from the loop header, and the following `post_ltr` run is never processed at all, so it stays at default `level` 0 / isolate level 0 from step 3. Those two level-0 tail runs become the later crashing pair.

The isolate-link builder connects runs by isolate level, not by list adjacency. For the witness tail it creates iso0 chain `pre_ltr -> fsi -> post_ltr` and iso1 chain `dagger -> newline`; in particular `post_ltr->prev_isolate = fsi` and `fsi->next_isolate = post_ltr` at this point.

At the first `compact_neutrals(main_run_list)` call at line 1037, `fsi` and `dagger` are adjacent, both neutral, both level 124, and their `run->bracket_type` fields from step 3 are `FRIBIDI_NO_BRACKET`, so this predicate merges them even though their isolate levels are 0 and 1. This is the earlier cross-isolate compaction the patch's second hunk forbids.

Merging `dagger` into `fsi` frees the `dagger` run and rewires only `dagger`'s isolate links: line 85 sets `newline->prev_isolate = NULL`, and line 94 sets `fsi->next_isolate = newline`. `post_ltr->prev_isolate` is not touched because `post_ltr` was the old iso0 successor of `fsi`, not `dagger->next_isolate`, so the stale-alias precursor is now `post_ltr->prev_isolate == fsi` while `fsi->next_isolate` no longer points back to `post_ltr`.

N0 finds no bracket pair in this witness, then lines 1213-1216 overwrite every surviving run's `bracket_type` with `FRIBIDI_NO_BRACKET` and re-run `compact_neutrals()`. For this witness no new same-level neutral pair exists, so the list shape stays `pre_ltr -> merged fsi+dagger -> newline -> post_ltr`, but the later line-1261 `RL_BRACKET_TYPE(...) == FRIBIDI_NO_BRACKET` checks now depend on this re-cleared state in the reviewed tree.

In N1/N2, the merged `fsi+dagger` run is still neutral. `get_adjacent_run()` sees `pre_ltr` behind it at the same level, and its forward isolate link now points to `newline`; because `newline->isolate_level > fsi->isolate_level`, lines 165-169 skip that cross-isolate run to the sentinel, so both sides resolve to `LTR`. Line 1255 rewrites the merged run to `LTR`, making the first line-1261 pair `pre_ltr` + merged `fsi+dagger` both `LTR` at level 124.

In the second `compact_list(main_run_list)` call at line 1261, `pre_ltr` and the merged `fsi+dagger` run now match on type `LTR`, level 124, and step 10's `FRIBIDI_NO_BRACKET` state, so `compact_list()` enters `merge_with_prev()` on that pair. This is the freeing merge recorded in the ASan free stack at `compact_list -> fribidi_get_par_embedding_levels_ex:1261`.

Sink. In `merge_with_prev(post_ltr)`, `second->prev_isolate` is still the freed `fsi` run from step 14, so line 93 writes `next_isolate` through that dangling pointer. This matches the saved ASan `heap-use-after-free WRITE of size 8` at `merge_with_prev:93`.
